issues.description: The solution implementation declares the screen buffer symbol as 'screen_buffer' but the problem statement and the template expect the symbol 'display_start'. The solution nevertheless references 'display_start' when computing/writing pixel addresses. This name mismatch will cause an undefined symbol / assembly error and confuses students about the required global buffer name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the buffer symbol consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the solution's declaration 'screen_buffer' to 'display_start', or update all references and the problem statement/template to use 'screen_buffer'. Prefer restoring 'display_start' in the solution's .bss section to match the template and problem description.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template refer to the screen base address as display_start. In the solution, the BSS section declares the buffer as screen_buffer but the code still uses the identifier display_start when computing addresses. This introduces a naming mismatch across artifacts (and an internal inconsistency in the solution) that hampers students' ability to map the problem requirement (use display_start) to the provided solution implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier for the framebuffer base across all artifacts. Rename the BSS symbol in the solution from screen_buffer to display_start (or update the template/problem to use screen_buffer). Ensure all references in the solution (e.g., add eax, display_start and mov esi, display_start) match the declared symbol name.
